subject: Unexpected prefetch loop — unscheduled micro-patch and verification steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Richards <emma.richards@greenline.ai>, support@greenline.ai
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-15T03:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected prefetch loop — immediate micro-patch proposed

Hi Emma / GreenLine team,

Quick heads-up from our side — overnight monitoring alerted us to a small regression in the prefetch path that can cause repeated prefix fetches for a minority of long-context requests. Impact is elevated token usage and increased tail latency for affected calls. We’ve scoped this to a narrow set of model + request-size combinations and seen it in ~0.7% of production requests for your account during the 02:30–02:55 PDT window.

We’re preparing a targeted micro-patch that fixes the loop in the prefetch state machine (no model reload required). The deployment is short (estimated 6–10 minutes) and stateless; it updates the runtime binary and clears a small in-memory cache shard. Expected customer-visible effects: reduced token duplication and quicker tail latency recovery.

Planned immediate steps (if you’re OK with us proceeding in the 15–30 minute window):
- Push hotfix to one region replica, smoke test with synthetic traffic (3–5m)
- Gradual rollout across remaining replicas (total ~10m)
- Post-deploy verification checklist run (I’ll share results)

If you prefer we can coordinate a slightly later maintenance window, but to limit token waste we recommend a short, immediate patch. Please reply with a quick ACK or any constraints.

Attachments: hotfix_prefetch_v1.patch (diff), verification-checklist.md

—
Markus Klein
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Emma Richards <emma.richards@greenline.ai>, support@greenline.ai
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-08-15T03:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected prefetch loop — immediate micro-patch proposed

ACK from ops — we can deploy on the 03:30 PDT window you proposed. I’ve staged the patch in canary and run the unit/regression test matrix against the prefetch suite. Summary: patch removes an extra conditional that re-enqueues items when a partial-kv state is seen; it adds a guard and an invariant check. No model files changed.

Deploy timeline (updates will be pushed to the channel):
- 03:30 PDT: deploy to canary replica (canary traffic at 2% for 3 minutes)
- 03:33 PDT: smoke tests (throughput and tail-latency sweep)
- 03:38–03:40 PDT: staged rollout to remainder (rolling restarts per replica)
- 03:45 PDT: verification-checklist complete and metrics snapshot attached

I’ll attach the hotfix diff and the checklist to the ticket. If we detect any anomalous regression we will immediately rollback.

Attachments: hotfix_prefetch_v1.patch, verification-checklist.md

—
Dev Patel
SRE Engineer, Runtime Reliability

Date: 2029-08-15T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Post-deploy summary and next steps — prefetch micro-patch

Emma — thanks again for the quick ACK. Final results and next steps: 

What we did:
- Deployed hotfix_prefetch_v1.patch across the affected region starting 03:30 PDT; rolling restarts per replica completed by 03:46 PDT.
- No model reloads or persistent-data writes; only an in-memory cache shard clear performed on each replica.

Observed outcome:
- Token duplication rate for the previously affected signature dropped from ~0.7% to <0.01% in 30 minutes.
- p95 tail latency for the sample workload improved by 16–20% post-fix.
- No customer-facing 5xx errors or retries attributable to the change.

Answering your questions:
1) No logs are retroactively modified. The fix alters runtime behavior going forward; historical request traces remain unchanged.
2) We will flag this event with your account manager (Lauren Bishop) to evaluate a discretionary credit for excess tokens consumed during the incident window. Lauren — please take this as the handoff for procurement/credit coordination.

Next steps and artifacts:
- Postmortem draft (internal) attached: postmortem-draft.txt
- Runbook updates: submitted PR to ops-runbooks (link above) to add the invariant check and a new smoke test.
- Customer verification checklist results: verification-checklist.md attached.

We’ll follow up with a final postmortem in 72 hours including root cause analysis, timeline, and preventive actions. If you’d like an earlier call to review the patch and telemetry, Lauren can coordinate.

Again, sorry for the inconvenience — appreciate your patience.

—
Markus Klein
Director, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
